text_blocks.snippet: RCC, or Renal Cell Carcinoma, is the most common type of kidney cancer, developing in the lining of the tiny tubes in the kidney that filter blood and produce urine. These tubes are called renal tubules. It's essentially a cancer that originates in the cells of the kidney.

list.title: Kidney Cancer Overview:
list.snippet: Kidney cancer, including RCC, is the abnormal growth of cells in the kidney tissue.

list.title: RCC Specifics:
list.snippet: Renal Cell Carcinoma (RCC) is the most frequent form of kidney cancer, accounting for the majority of kidney cancer cases.

list.title: Location:
list.snippet: RCC arises from the cells lining the renal tubules, which are crucial for filtering blood and producing urine.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: RCC can manifest with various symptoms, including weight loss, low-grade fever, bone pain, and high blood pressure.

list.title: Risk Factors:
list.snippet: Some factors that may increase the risk of RCC include smoking, obesity, high blood pressure, family history, and exposure to certain toxins.

list.title: Types of RCC:
list.snippet: There are different types of RCC, including clear cell, papillary, and chromophobe RCC. Papillary RCC, for example, has two subtypes, type 1 (slow-growing) and type 2 (aggressive).

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Treatment options for RCC depend on the stage and type of cancer, and may include surgery, radiation, targeted therapy, or immunotherapy.
